title: Continuous glucose monitor sensor
what: A small sensor sticks to the skin and shows your sugar around the clock on a phone or reader. You need to prick your finger much less often.
why: With diabetes, to see your sugar all the time, including at night.
duration: putting it on takes a few minutes; a sensor usually works for 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: If you often have low sugar, especially at night
If the skin under the plaster gets irritated
If you are due for an MRI, CT, or X-ray, since the sensor is usually removed
If the sensor readings differ from your glucose meter

prepare.title: Site
prepare.text: Usually the upper arm or the belly, as the instructions say. The skin should be clean, without scars or moles.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Wipe the spot with an alcohol wipe and let it dry. Do not put creams on that spot.

prepare.title: Phone
prepare.text: Install the app beforehand and make sure your phone is charged.

prepare.title: Meter
prepare.text: Keep your glucose meter, as you need it if how you feel does not match the sensor numbers.

steps: Wash your hands and check the sensor's expiry date
Wipe your skin with alcohol and wait until it dries
Prepare the applicator following the instructions
Press the applicator against the skin and push, so the sensor attaches
Carefully remove the applicator and smooth down the plaster
Connect the sensor in the app
Wait for the warm-up time, as the first numbers do not appear right away
feel: You notice the sensor on your skin for the first hours, then get used to it
after: Do not catch the sensor on clothing, and take care in doorways and with bags
You can usually swim and shower, but check the instructions
If numbers look odd, check your sugar with the meter
Show the graphs to your doctor, who uses them to adjust treatment
red_flags: Shakiness, sweating, or confusion: check your sugar and eat something sweet, even if the sensor shows normal
Redness, pain, or pus under the sensor: remove it and see a doctor
A person is unconscious or having seizures: call emergency services

faq.q: Do I still need to prick my finger?
faq.a: Much less often. Check by finger if how you feel does not match the numbers, or if the sensor asks.

faq.q: Why does the sensor show different numbers than the meter?
faq.a: The sensor measures sugar in the fluid under the skin, and it lags by a few minutes. A small difference is normal.

reminders.text: Your sensor expires tomorrow. Have a new one ready, along with alcohol wipes.
